scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported 1878 polygon is a map snapshot, not the 1822 independent state founding. No geometry or Indigenous territorial accuracy is certified.

Empire, republic and later regimes are phases of a continuing state, while Indigenous and quilombola communities have distinct histories. Household, school and cultural examples do not imply uniform conditions across Brazil.
The original Portuguese excerpt is from the 1988 Constitution; it does not represent all written or spoken languages in Brazil. Narrative awaits independent review.

proposedOverrides.summary: Brazil became an independent empire in 1822 and a republic in 1889; the imported map begins only in 1878. Its history includes slavery and abolition, industrial growth, public-health research, two dictatorships and the 1988 constitution. Indigenous and quilombola communities, many languages and regional cultural practices continue. Brazil remains a republic; changing governments did not end its peoples or state.

identityEvidence.assessment: Imported label/interval confirmed; border and Indigenous-territory accuracy unverified.
